summary:
S. 2336, the "Halting the Epidemic of Addiction and Loss Act of 2025," directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to ensure that references to opioid overdose reversal agents in specified HHS grant programs are not limited to naloxone, but instead encompass any opioid overdose reversal drug approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Section 2(a) imposes a prospective mandate on the Secretary. Whenever the Department of Health and Human Services issues a regulation or guidance for any grant program addressing opioid misuse and use disorders, the Secretary must ensure, as appropriate, that any reference to an opioid overdose reversal drug is inclusive of any such drug approved under section 505 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 355) for emergency treatment of a known or suspected opioid overdose.

Section 2(b) addresses preexisting regulations and guidance. It requires the Secretary, not later than one year after the date of enactment, to update all existing references to opioid overdose reversal drugs to be inclusive of any opioid overdose reversal drug approved or otherwise authorized for use by the FDA. This update requirement applies to references in HHS regulations or guidance issued prior to enactment that pertain to two specific grant programs: (1) the grant program for State and Tribal response to opioid use disorders under section 1003 of the 21st Century Cures Act (42 U.S.C. 290ee-3a), commonly known as State and Tribal Opioid Response Grants; and (2) the grant program for priority substance use disorder prevention needs of regional and national significance under section 516 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 290bb-22).

The Act establishes a directive to an executive agency and does not provide new authorizations of appropriations or establish new grant programs. The effective date of the prospective mandate is the date of enactment, while the statutory deadline for updating existing references is set at one year post-enactment.
